comment.body: Keyboard Manager currently requires a shortcut to contain at least one modifier and a non-modifier action key, so Ctrl+Shift alone is intentionally rejected. This is documented and explicitly tested, even though Windows/Notepad can use modifier-only gestures. Supporting suppression of that gesture would need a separate design that preserves longer combinations such as Ctrl+Shift+Arrow; simply bypassing editor validation is not a safe fix. Remapping a modifier globally is also not equivalent to disabling only this Notepad gesture.

known_information: The requested source shortcut is only Ctrl+Shift, to suppress Notepad reading-direction changes.
Official Keyboard Manager documentation requires a modifier and a non-modifier action key.
EditorHelpers.IsValidShortcut requires an action key and the existing IsValidShortcut_ShouldReturnFalse_OnPassingShortcutWithOnlyModifierKeys test explicitly covers Ctrl+Shift.
inferences: A future modifier-only feature would need release-time/longer-shortcut semantics; accepting the row without that design could interfere with ordinary selection shortcuts.
issue_context.summary: Modifier-only shortcut capture is outside the current Keyboard Manager shortcut grammar.
issue_context.analysis: The editor is following its supported grammar, not failing to record an ordinary supported shortcut. Supporting modifier-only release gestures requires a separate interaction design so Ctrl+Shift+Arrow and other longer combinations still work.

title: Unable to remap shortcuts that contain only modifier keys like notepad's Ctrl + Shift

judgment.recommended_action: Explain the current limitation and treat modifier-only suppression as a feature request, not a local validation bypass.
